QUANTITATIVE SUPPORT FOR ROUTING QUERY-FIRST, measured while testing the budget guard.

Same request, same frame, same pairing:

  materialized     conservative memory plan requires 111360 bytes
  query-first      the same request requires  59300 bytes

A 47 percent reduction. So the wrapper rule on this bead - route through plan_geometry and the existing query-first branch, never call geometry() - is not only semantically safe, it is materially cheaper in workspace. That is an argument for the design that is independent of ergonomics and independent of the semantic argument, and it partly offsets the cost caveat recorded here earlier: query-first pays per query in TIME but needs roughly half the workspace in MEMORY.

The full trade, now measured on both axes:
  materialized   more memory, amortizes across questions      good for many questions
  query-first    less memory, pays per question               good for one question, or when
                                                              workspace is the binding constraint

That second row is the case the one-liner serves, and it is a real case on brain-scale data where workspace is exactly what binds.
